title: cmdpal dock new auto-hide bug with bottom position
summary: A new current-package reproduction and source inspection support a bottom-edge reveal loop: the hit test has no upper Y bound, so taskbar positions can keep satisfying reveal after collapse is allowed.
next_action: Reproduce the bottom-dock/taskbar loop on the installed package, then consider approval of the bounded edge-hit-test proposal.

judgment.rationale: The deterministic original sequence is now supported by a detailed reproduction on package 0.13.13001.0 and focused source evidence. IsCursorAtDockEdge's Bottom branch checks only a lower Y bound plus X-in-rect; CanCollapseAutoHideDock allows collapse when the cursor is below the revealed rectangle. The mechanism is plausible, while the author's isolated candidate checks are not a full app build or integration verification.
evidence: The original sequence is Bottom position, Auto-hide on, pointer into the Windows taskbar; the Dock repeatedly shows/hides instead of remaining stable.
The 2026-10-28 comment reports the behavior on Command Palette package 0.13.13001.0, Windows 11 26H2 build 26300.9711, Bottom position and Auto-hide on, with a stationary pointer over the taskbar.
Current DockWindow.xaml.cs Bottom reveal predicate checks cursor.Y >= _revealedRect.bottom - margin and X within the rect, but has no upper Y bound.
CanCollapseAutoHideDock uses IsPointInRect(_revealedRect, cursorPoint) to block collapse only when the pointer is inside the revealed rectangle, supporting the reveal/collapse asymmetry.
The reporter reports 1,200 isolated hit-test cases but explicitly says no full application build/test and multi-monitor/fullscreen behavior remains unverified.
No covering upstream issue/PR, assignee, or fork issue/PR/branch trace was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Verify the bottom-taskbar interaction on the installed package and retain valid edge activation; then approve only the bounded hit-test design, not an unvalidated implementation.

issue_context.summary: Bottom-docked Command Palette auto-hide repeatedly reveals and collapses when the pointer rests in the Windows taskbar area.
known_information: The original reproduction sets Dock position to Bottom, enables auto-hide, and moves the pointer into the taskbar.
The latest comment supplies current package version, Windows build, monitor/settings state, and stationary-pointer reproduction.
The Bottom reveal predicate has no upper Y bound; collapse is blocked only when the pointer is inside the actual revealed rectangle and WindowFromPoint resolves to the Dock window.
The reported isolated hit-test checks did not build or exercise the full application.
inferences: A pointer in the taskbar below the revealed Dock may continue satisfying the Bottom reveal predicate after collapse while collapse logic sees it outside the rectangle, producing oscillation.
Constraining reveal detection to the Dock rectangle is likely to address the loop, but valid edge activation and multi-monitor/fullscreen behavior need integration verification.
issue_context.analysis: The 2026-10-28 comment adds a current-package reproduction and source-grounded explanation. Reuse it rather than requesting logs or repeating earlier investigation. The change remains a design candidate because only an isolated check, not an application build, was reported.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue and all three comments; older comments add one matching video and a broader request about additional taskbar positions.
Read DockWindow.xaml.cs around IsCursorAtDockEdge and CanCollapseAutoHideDock; verified the missing upper coordinate bound and rectangle-limited collapse check.
Reused the reporter's disclosed 1,200-case isolated test result without rerunning tests or building; the comment says integration behavior remains unverified.
Searched upstream related PRs/issues and MuyuanMS fork issue/PR/branch traces; no covering work or assignee was found.

fix_assessment.rationale: The reveal predicate's unbounded coordinate and rectangle-based collapse test explain the reported oscillation. The candidate must preserve activation at valid edge positions and be verified across dock sides and monitor/taskbar layouts.

proposed_fixes.title: Bound auto-hide reveal detection to the dock edge rectangle
proposed_fixes.root_cause: For Bottom docking, IsCursorAtDockEdge accepts any cursor Y at or below the dock's bottom edge as long as X remains within the dock width. A pointer in the taskbar below the revealed rectangle can trigger reveal even though CanCollapseAutoHideDock considers it outside and allows collapse.
plan: Constrain edge reveal detection to the revealed Dock rectangle before applying the side-specific edge-margin test.
Preserve the intended one-pixel activation margin and verify equivalent behavior for Top, Left, and Right edges.
Add regression coverage for a cursor in the taskbar below Bottom docking and valid edge activation on single- and multi-monitor layouts.
verification: With Bottom docking and auto-hide enabled, leave the cursor stationary in the taskbar and verify the Dock does not oscillate.
Move across the valid Dock edge and verify reveal still works; repeat with alternate taskbar settings, dock sides, and monitor layouts.

confidence.rationale: The control-flow asymmetry directly matches the stationary-taskbar symptom, but full application behavior and edge activation regressions have not been tested.

actions.label: Approve bounded Dock auto-hide hit-test proposal
Reproduce Bottom Dock taskbar oscillation
actions.note: The reporter supplied a deterministic current-package sequence; verify full-app edge behavior before design handoff.

reproduce.title: Verify Bottom Dock auto-hide near the taskbar
setup: Use one enabled primary display with the Windows taskbar at the bottom.
Set Always on top on and use Compact Dock size as in the detailed report.
steps: Restart Command Palette with Bottom docking and Auto-hide enabled.
Place the pointer over the bottom taskbar and leave it stationary.
Observe whether the Dock repeatedly reveals and collapses.
Move the pointer to the actual Dock edge and confirm valid reveal still works.
reproduce.expected_result: The Dock remains stable while the pointer is over the taskbar and reveals only when the pointer enters its valid activation edge.
